doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

title: Record collection and daughter compiling his work
summary: May has no copies of his records; his second wife found CDs online and his daughter is compiling his discography.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Right. So Billy and I were the house trio, Billy’s trio was at this place called the Downbeat, which used to be on 54th Street. And Oscar was a regular. We got to play with everybody in that place you know. Bill Harris came in, he was one of the featured —J.J. Johnson you know. We were the house trio. So I’d sit behind Oscar when he was playing. And then at night after the end of the gig, he and I would go in all these after hour joints and hang out and play and stuff.
Do you have copies of all the records you played on?

No. My second wife called me yesterday and told me that, “You know there’s about 40 CDs or 44 CDs of yours on the internet.” I said well wonderful. So she just sent me copies. But I don’t have the records. My youngest daughter is trying to compile everything that I’ve done, just for family reasons.
Sure. That would jog your memory too I bet.
